# Swim & Lift (v6.1)

*Chest & Arms Micro-Sessions | Swimmer Program (Age 56)*

Last updated 2026-09-03.

| Fasted Swim | Gym Frequency | Session Length | Joint Safety |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2,300m (07:00-08:30) | 3 Days / Week | 20-25 min Micro-Session | Rotator Cuff Focus |

## Daily Timing Protocol

| Time Window | Activity / Event | Nutritional & Recovery Strategy |
| --- | --- | --- |

| 07:00-08:30 | 2,300m Fasted Swim (90 mins) | Maintain steady cadence. 1,500m Freestyle pulls heavy on internal rotators; 800m Backstroke counters chest tightness. Doubles as the full thermal and joint warm-up for the gym. |

| 09:15 | Post-Workout Breakfast | Full recovery meal: 35g-40g protein + complex carbs (e.g., 4 eggs + oatmeal or a whey smoothie). This is the real refuel, once the training is done. |

## Locker-Room Transition Fuel (08:30)

**Recipe:** 200-250ml (0.20-0.25 L) Leche Desnatada Omega-3 + 1 tbsp Miel Pura, plus an optional pinch of salt.

**Why:** Restores blood glucose and halts muscle breakdown immediately following 90 minutes of fasted swimming. Small enough to drink in the five minutes it takes to change, so there is no stomach sloshing or heaviness under a loaded bar minutes later.

---

## Warm-Up & Cool-Down

### Warm-Up Protocol - The 2,300m Swim Is the Warm-Up

The 5-8 minute rowing machine ergometer warm-up is removed. 90 minutes of swimming has already raised core temperature and lubricated the shoulder joints, and the 25-minute window has no room to spare. Go directly to the first lift after 1 light prep set at roughly half the working weight.

### Cool-Down & Spinal Decompression - Passive Bar Dead Hangs

- **Timing:** End of every gym session (mandatory).
- **Why:** Heavy pressing and rowing compress the spine and tighten the upper back and shoulders. A dead hang reverses that compression, relaxes tight muscles, and resets posture.
- **How to do it:** 1 set of 60 seconds. Keep it passive - relax and let gravity pull the hips down. This is the one part of the session that is never skipped for time.

---

## Rules of Training & Joint Safety (Age 56)

**1. The 3-Second Eccentric Rule (Controlled Barbell Lowering)**

At age 56, lowering heavy barbell weight uncontrollably increases shoulder and elbow tendon wear without extra muscle gain. Lower every bench press and curl over 3 slow seconds to maximize mechanical muscle tension while keeping joints completely safe.

**2. Barbell Pressing Path & Scapular Retraction**

Never press with flared elbows (90 degrees). On both the Flat and Incline Barbell Bench Press, tuck elbows to a 45-60 degree angle to the torso and keep shoulder blades pinched tightly together into the bench. This isolates the pecs and protects the rotator cuffs from swimmer's impingement.

**3. Keep 1 to 2 Reps in Reserve (RPE 8 Training Threshold)**

Do not train to absolute muscle failure on barbell presses. End the set when 1 or 2 more clean reps are still possible. This preserves central nervous system recovery for the 7:00 AM daily swims - and inside a 25-minute window, a set taken to failure costs more rest time than the extra rep is worth.

**4. Posterior Shoulder Counter-Balance**

Freestyle swimming and barbell chest pressing both tighten internal rotators (pectoralis major & lats). Never skip Rear Delt Flyes or Seated Rows - they pull the shoulder heads back into optimal joint alignment.

---

## Leg Training Is Deliberately Omitted

No leg exercises are performed in the gym. Lower-body volume is already fully covered by daily swim kicks, running and tennis. Adding squats or leg presses to a 25-minute post-swim window would compete directly with recovery for the next morning's 2,300m swim, which is the foundation the whole program is built on.

## The Sessions

### Day 1: Flat Chest Mass & Push Focus

*Flat barbell chest, machine press volume, outer tricep, rear delts*

**B1 - Flat Barbell Bench Press** **[Key Compound]**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 6-8 Reps
- **Target:** Overall Chest / Sternal Pecs, Delts & Triceps
- **Tempo:** 3s Lower | 1s Pause | Explosive Press
- **Cues:**
    - Lock in scapular retraction (pinch shoulder blades down & back into bench).
    - Lower bar to mid-lower sternum; press upward in slight arc toward eye level.
    - Keep 45 degree elbow tuck to protect swimmer's rotator cuff joints.

**A3 - Flat Machine Chest Press**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 10-12 Reps
- **Target:** Main Chest / Sternal Pecs
- **Tempo:** 2s Lower | 1s Controlled Squeeze
- **Cues:**
    - Provides safe hyper-isolation volume following heavy barbell benching.
    - Focus on squeezing inner chest together without locking elbows hard.

**A5 - Cable Rope Tricep Pushdown**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 10-12 Reps
- **Target:** Triceps Lateral / Outer Head
- **Tempo:** Dynamic | 1s Split Hold
- **Cues:**
    - Pin elbows tight to torso; pull rope handles apart at bottom lockout.
    - Never do this before the pressing work - fresh triceps are what hold up the bench press.

**A6 - Reverse Pec Deck (Rear Delt Fly)**

- **Prescription:** 2 Sets x 12-15 Reps
- **Target:** Rear Deltoids & Rotator Cuff
- **Benefit:** Essential post-swim joint safety
- **Cues:**
    - Sit facing pad. Drive handles backward using rear shoulders.
    - Protects shoulders against swimmer's forward posture imbalance.

### Day 2: Upper Back & Biceps Peak

*Upper back thickness, biceps peak, brachialis*

**B2 - Chest-Supported Machine Row (or Seated Cable Row)**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 8-10 Reps
- **Target:** Upper Back & Rear Shoulders
- **Benefit:** Zero lower back strain; 100% upper back
- **Cues:**
    - Drive elbows outward wide to balance heavy swim pulling forces.
    - Keep chest firmly pressed against pad throughout entire set.
    - If the machine is taken, use the seated cable row with a neutral grip: pull the handle to the belly button while driving the shoulder blades together.
    - Heavier 8-10 range in v6.0 - this is now the only compound pull of the week.

**A4 - Standing Supinating Dumbbell Curls**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 10-12 Reps
- **Target:** Biceps Brachii (Peak Zone)
- **Tempo:** Smooth Curl | 2s Descent
- **Cues:**
    - Keep elbows stationary at your sides; turn palm outward at peak contraction.
    - Avoid body swing to keep tension strictly on biceps.

**B4 - Dumbbell Hammer Curls**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 10-12 Reps
- **Target:** Brachialis & Forearms
- **Grip:** Neutral thumb-up for arm width
- **Cues:**
    - Pushes biceps upward for thicker overall arm appearance.
    - Avoid swinging; lower under complete control (2-3 seconds).

### Day 3: Upper Chest, Triceps & Posterior Shoulder

*Incline barbell chest, inner chest, tricep long head, posterior delts*

**A1 - Incline Barbell Bench Press** **[Key Compound]**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 6-8 Reps
- **Target:** Upper Chest / Clavicular Pecs & Front Delts
- **Tempo:** 3s Lower | 1s Touch | 1s Press
- **Cues:**
    - Set bench angle strictly to 30 degrees (minimizes front shoulder strain).
    - Tuck elbows at 45 to 60 degrees to body; do not flare out to 90 degrees.
    - Touch bar to upper collarbone/sternum area without bouncing off chest.

**B3 - Pec Deck Machine Fly**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 10-12 Reps
- **Target:** Inner Sternal Chest / Mid Pecs
- **Tempo:** 2s Stretch | 1s Squeeze | 2s Return
- **Cues:**
    - Sit facing away from the machine; adjust seat height so handles align directly with mid-chest.
    - Maintain a slight, rigid flex in elbows; drive handles together in front of sternum, squeezing hard for 1 second at peak contraction.
    - Provides smooth, continuous mechanical tension across pecs with zero lower back or wrist instability.

**B5 - Seated DB Overhead Tricep Extension**

- **Prescription:** 3 Sets x 10-12 Reps
- **Target:** Triceps Long Head
- **Benefit:** Maximum long-head stretch with zero cable setup
- **Cues:**
    - Sit on a backed bench; cup one dumbbell overhead with both hands, elbows pointing forward.
    - Lower behind head until the long head is fully stretched (3 seconds), then press up cleanly.
    - Keep upper arms fixed next to ears and ribs down; do not let elbows flare wide.

**B6 - Reverse Pec Deck (Machine Rear Delt Fly)**

- **Prescription:** 2 Sets x 12-15 Reps
- **Target:** Posterior Deltoids & Rotator Cuff
- **Benefit:** Posterior delt shield against swim strain
- **Cues:**
    - Sit facing the chest pad; keep chest against the pad and shoulder blades stable.
    - Drive handles backward wide using the rear shoulders to shield rotator cuffs against swim strain.

## Equipment Availability & Exercise Swapping

> B1 (Flat Barbell Bench Press, Day 1) and A1 (Incline Barbell Bench Press, Day 3) are non-negotiable anchor lifts to be done first. Because they use heavy loads in the 6-8 rep range, doing them late in a 25-minute session after the chest and triceps are fatigued increases injury risk and degrades strength gains.

**1. High Priority (Do 1st)**

- **B1 & A1:** Always secure the bench rack first, while the central nervous system is still fresh from the swim.
- **B2:** Day 2's only compound pull, so it opens the session. If the chest-supported machine is occupied, switch to the seated cable row - same 8-10 prescription, no waiting.

**2. Medium Priority (Flexible Middle Moves)**

- **A3 & B3:** Machine chest volume in the 10-12 range. If the machine is busy, move to that day's tricep or rear delt work and come back - the strength progression lives on the barbell, not here.

**3. Fully Swappable (Do Anywhere Near the End)**

- **A5 & B5:** A5 is the only exercise left that needs a free cable station and rope; B5 needs only a dumbbell and a backed bench, so it never waits on equipment. Golden rule: never do tricep isolation before that day's pressing (B1/A3 on Day 1, A1 on Day 3).
- **A4 & B4:** Pure arm isolation. Can be done in any empty space with dumbbells during the second half of Day 2.
- **A6 & B6:** Day 1 and Day 3 both finish on the reverse pec deck. Low-risk, high-rep isolation that fits almost any open slot; if the machine is taken, substitute a bench-supported dumbbell rear delt fly.

> **The Golden Rule:** In a 25-minute window there is no time to queue for a machine. If the rack is not open for B1/A1, start with that day's machine work or rear delts and come back to the bar - just hold off on tricep isolation until the pressing is done.

## Summary Strategy

The 7:00 AM swim is the untouchable physical and mental foundation, and in v6.0 it also serves as the warm-up. Five minutes of locker-room fuel bridges it to a 20-25 minute gym micro-session three mornings a week, so all ten exercises still get their full volume in sessions short enough to sustain on top of daily swimming. Heavy compound barbell pressing drives upper body mass, strict upper back pulling and posterior shoulder isolation keep the joints aligned against swimmer's forward posture, and every session closes with a 60-second passive dead hang. Legs are trained by the pool, the road and the tennis court, never in the gym.
